Abstract—Agriculture plays a key role in security of 
food, rural livelihoods and sustainable use of resources, 
particularly in India where many farmers face crucial 
decisions on crop choice, fertilizer use, irrigation and pest 
management amid climatic variability and limited access to 
experts.

periodic soil testing and extension visits are often too slow 
and fragmented to support timely, field -level decisions 
throughout the crop cycle. AI and ML can be used to study 
large datasets from agriculture to find the links between 
environmental factors with outcomes such as suitable crops, 
soil fertility, yields and disease.

The proposed system architecture is modular in which three 
functions share a data layer but apply different models to process 
the input data type. Soil analysis and crop recommendation is 
done based on tabular data (input parameters: nutrient contents, 
pH, rainfall, temperature and humidity) whereas disease 
detection is done based on imagery.

continuous process that runs in parallel with the

II. MODULE 1: CROP RECOMMENDATION 
A. Objective 
The crop recommendation module recommends the best crop 
that has to be cultivated in a particular land based on the 
amount of nutrients present in the soil such as Nitrogen, 
Phosphorus and Potassium, pH level in the soil and climate 
including temperature, humidity and rainfall. B. Methodology 
The crop recommendation module is a multi -class 
classification problem.

these implementations is to train Random Forest, Support 
Vector Machine and Gradient Boosting classifiers on a 
labeled dataset that relates a combination of aforementioned 
features to a certain crop.22 Classifiers such as Random Forests 
are primarily used because they are robust to noisy measurement 
typical of sensor readings and allow us to determine which

A. Objective 
The soil analysis module classifies soil samples by type (e.g., 
alluvial, black, red, laterite) and fertility status, providing the 
nutrient and physicochemical context required both for direct 
fertilisation guidance and as an upstream input to the crop 
recommendation module. B. Methodology 
Two distinct methodologies were employed in the 
study. The first included the use of standard ML classifiers 
(as in Module 1) to classify physicochemical properties 
acquired from sensor readings (moisture, EC, pH, N-PK).

d the use of standard ML classifiers 
(as in Module 1) to classify physicochemical properties 
acquired from sensor readings (moisture, EC, pH, N-PK). The second methodology comprised the utilization of C 
NNs to process texture and color information from images of 
soil samples, which allowed, in some cases, the classification 
of the soil type directly from the 
images, thus providing an alternative in situations when the 
latter are unavailable, or when IoT or lab equipment is not 
available. The features were subjected to scaling and 
normalisation, as nutrient values varied in a considerably 
wide range. C. Results and Discussion

The core of the system we are developing is to use 
artificial intelligence to identify crop diseases, and 
complete detection based on images of plant leaves.The 
goal of this system is very clear: it must accurately detect 
problems with crops in the early stage, when diseases have 
just emerged and not yet spread.

of this system is very clear: it must accurately detect 
problems with crops in the early stage, when diseases have 
just emerged and not yet spread. It must not only recognize 
that a crop is ill, but also distinguish and categorize different 
diseases one by one to complete proper classification.With 
the support of this system, farmers can take timely 
prevention and control measures before diseases break out 
on a large scale. They will not have to watch helplessly as 
diseases spread and destroy the crops across an entire field. This can significantly reduce crop losses, and ultimately

The current study proposes a holistic approach to 
effectively integrate smart and sustainable agriculture 
through the use of soll analysis, crop selection, 
estimating yield, optimizing irrigation, and disease 
management.

mart and sustainable agriculture 
through the use of soll analysis, crop selection, 
estimating yield, optimizing irrigation, and disease 
management. The technologies proposed in this framework 
collectively facilitate data -based decisions during the 
production cycle of crops to make it easier for farmers to 
choose the right crops, optimize water and other agricultural 
input, increase efficiency, and detect diseases in 
advance.The designed framework is of great use for both 
small and large farmers by avoiding unnecessary irrigation 
and chemical intervention and imp roving the harvesting 
process. It lets small farmers take informed decisions 
regarding their activities at an affordable cost, and large 
ones develop specific and automated resource management 
methodology.

can be raised, the utilization rate of resources indispensable 
to farming such as water a nd fertilizers can be improved, 
and the entire path of agricultural development can be made 
more sustainable, eliminating the need to sacrifice the 
environment for short-term harvests.
